name: Gnoll
summary: Gnolls are a savage, hyena-like race of humanoid scavengers and raiders found scattered across both the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. Renowned for their vicious infighting, brutal strength, and animal cunning, they survive by pillaging settlements, butchering wildlife, and ambushing unwary travelers. Left unchecked, their sprawling packs and warlords pose a constant threat to frontier hamlets and trade roads alike.

sections.title: Hyenas of the Wilds
sections.body: Standing slightly shorter than the average human but possessing explosive physical power, gnolls are bipedal hyena-kin known for their spiky teeth, thick pelts, and distinct barking laugh. While fully capable of walking upright, they often drop to all fours to lope swiftly through brush or track prey by scent. Gnoll culture values raw physical dominance above all else. They organize into fractious packs led by the strongest, cruelest alpha, only yielding when battered into submission by a superior force.

sections.title: The Gnoll War
sections.body: Though usually fractured by petty squabbles, united gnolls once waged open war on the kingdom of Stormwind. Stormwind's armies prevailed in that Gnoll War, and the kingdom enjoyed a lasting peace afterward until the orcs came through the Dark Portal.

sections.title: Raiders of the Southern Kingdoms
sections.body: In the south, gnoll packs run rampant in the absence of Stormwind's full military might. In Elwynn Forest and Westfall, the Riverpaw pack—marshaled by the notorious Hogger—raids homesteads and forces subjugated kobolds to dig for gold, secretly colluding with the Defias Brotherhood. Further east in the Redridge Mountains, the Redridge pack snatches horses outside Lakeshire and sabotages bridge repairs, while the Shadowhide clan in Galardell Valley serves the dark will of the rogue wizard Morganth.

sections.title: Pestilence and Territory
sections.body: Gnoll menace is not limited to the human south. In northern Lordaeron, the Scourge necromancer Thule Ravenclaw raises undead Rot Hide gnolls to dig up corpses across Tirisfal and Silverpine. Near Hillsbrad, the Mudsnout harvest foul, toxic blossoms among ruined farmsteads. Across the Great Sea in Kalimdor, the Palemane pack butchers game across Mulgore despite tauren efforts to make peace, while the Woodpaw of Feralas wage a desperate, frenzied war against encroaching silithid swarms.

faq.answer: Gnolls are hyena-like humanoid carnivores known for their violent nature, physical endurance, and low cunning. They live in nomadic or semi-permanent camps, surviving mostly on plunder, hunting, and carrion.

faq.q: Why don't gnolls form a proper kingdom?
faq.answer: Gnolls are fiercely belligerent and driven by immediate hierarchy. Without an exceptional and tyrannical warlord beating them into line, packs inevitably splinter into bloody territorial feuds, preventing long-term organization or civil progress.

Long before the First War, united gnoll packs waged war on the kingdom of Stormwind. The kingdom's armies prevailed, and Stormwind enjoyed a lasting peace afterward until the orcs came through the Dark Portal.

faq.q: Why are gnolls working with the Defias Brotherhood?
faq.answer: The Riverpaw pack in Westfall and Elwynn collaborates with the Defias Brotherhood in exchange for arms, coordination, and shared spoils. The bandits use the gnolls as brute muscle to overrun farmlands and distract Stormwind's dwindling garrisons.

faq.q: Are the Rot Hide gnolls alive?
faq.answer: No. The Rot Hide gnolls prowling Tirisfal Glades and Silverpine Forest are undead thralls. They answer to Thule Ravenclaw, an exiled human necromancer using Fenris Isle as a redoubt to gather corpses for the Scourge.

faq.q: Why do tauren fight the Palemane gnolls?
faq.answer: When the tauren settled Mulgore, they attempted to coexist and communicate with the indigenous Palemane pack. The gnolls rebuffed all peaceful gestures, slaughtering the plains wildlife without restraint and threatening tauren villages.

angles.text: For humans of Stormwind, gnolls are an ancient enemy that once burned the kingdom's heartlands; today, packs like the Riverpaw and Shadowhide threaten the kingdom's vulnerable frontier roads.
The Palemane tribe in Mulgore treats the land with careless cruelty, forcing young tauren braves to drive them back to preserve the balance of the plains.
Alliance marshals across Elwynn, Westfall, Redridge, and the Wetlands rely heavily on freelance champions to thin out encroaching gnoll populations.
The Forsaken view gnolls either as an annoyance or a resource: the Mudsnout cultivate restorative fungi in Hillsbrad, while Sylvanas previously enslaved northern packs through banshee possession.
